headline: Route every prompt to the cheapest LLM with a Pydantic AI cost optimizer
summary: Stop overpaying for LLM API calls. A new approach uses a lightweight classifier to route prompts to the minimum sufficient model, potentially saving thousands monthly on unnecessary advanced reasoning.
details: Many teams overspend on LLM APIs by using a single, powerful model for all requests. For example, routing a simple "Is this email spam?" prompt to GPT-4o costs ~$0.015, while Groq can do it for ~$0.0001. Scaling this to 100,000 prompts daily can hemorrhage $1,400 per month.

The core problem isn't model selection, but dynamically routing each prompt to the minimum sufficient model without building fragile, hand-coded classification logic. This requires infrastructure that learns prompt complexity from data and automates routing decisions.

The proposed solution involves a three-layer architecture. Layer 1, Complexity Classification, uses a lightweight model like Claude Haiku to analyze incoming prompts and assign a complexity score. This classification cost is negligible compared to the potential savings.

Layer 2, Model Selection, then uses this classification output to pick the cheapest model that meets the prompt's requirements. Initially a lookup table, this layer becomes data-driven by tracking which models succeed at various complexity levels, optimizing routing rules over time.

Layer 3, Execution and Tracking, runs the prompt on the selected model, logging cost and latency. This data feeds back into a cost database, providing ground truth for continuous optimization. Pydantic-ai is recommended for its type-safe, structured outputs and agent-based workflow.

A key design decision is ensuring the complexity classification itself is cheap and fast, using models like Haiku and caching patterns to minimize overhead. LiteLLM serves as a unified interface for multiple providers like Claude, GPT-4o, and Groq.

This pattern separates concerns cleanly, isolating classification from routing logic, making model selection deterministic and auditable. Built-in cost tracking provides real-time visibility into spending patterns.

One important consideration is managing provider rate limits. A queue (e.g., Bull, Celery) is necessary to throttle requests by provider, preventing API limits from forcing prompts to more expensive fallback models when scaling.

This approach does introduce trade-offs, adding 200-500ms latency due to an extra LLM call for classification. Additionally, the routing map needs ongoing maintenance as new models launch or pricing structures change.

headline: 60% of TikTok videos are AI-generated 'slop', study finds
summary: A new study reveals that nearly 60% of videos on TikTok are AI-generated, with YouTube also seeing a significant portion of its content created by artificial intelligence.
details: A recent analysis by online video editing platform Kapwing has shed light on the prevalence of AI-generated content across major social media platforms.
The study found that a staggering 60% of videos on TikTok are classified as 'AI slop', indicating a massive influx of algorithmically created content.
YouTube is also affected, with the study reporting that 21% of its videos are AI-generated. This highlights a growing trend of AI adoption in content creation.
The term 'AI slop' suggests that much of this generated content may lack originality or quality, potentially impacting user experience and the authenticity of online media.
